questions.q: If a copper wire is stretched to increase its length by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>20</mn><mo>%</mo></math>. The percentage increase in resistance of the wire is _____%.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Before heating, resistance of wire is R0=ρl0A0

After heating, resistance is R=ρlA

As volume = constant

Therefore,

A0l0=1.2l0A

⇒A=A01.2

So,

R=ρlA=ρ×1.2l0A01.2=ρl0A0×1.44=1.44 R0

Percentage increase in R =R-R0R0×100=44%

questions.q: All resistances in figure are 1 Ω each. The value of current 'I' is a5 A. The value of a is _____ .
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Each pair on the right side of the circuit is in parallel connection, hence it can be replaced by a resistance of r2 as shown.

Now, r & r2 in each branch on the right side is in series, hence combined resistance value will be, 3r2. Upper branch having resistance 3r2 is in parallel with another 3r2, hence it can be written as 3r4.

Further, simplified circuit will have net resistance of 7r8.

Therefore, Req=7r8+r=78+1=158 Ω

Now, current I=3158=85 A

Hence, value of a=8.

questions.q: A potential V0 is applied across a uniform wire of resistance R. The power dissipation is P1. The wire is then cut into two equal halves and a potential of V0 is applied across the length of each half. The total power dissipation across two wires is P2. The ratio of P2:P1 is x:1. The value of x is _____.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The formula to calculate the power dissipated in the first case can be written as

P1=V02R   ...1

When the wire is halved, its resistance will also become half the previous value.

Thus, the formula to calculate the power dissipated in the second case can be written as

P2=V02R2×2= 4V02R   ...2

Divide equation (2) by equation (1) to calculate the required ratio.

P2P1=4V02RV02R=4=16

Hence, x=16.

The total current flowing through the loop,

I=VR'=9 V3 Ω=3 A

Thus, through each branch the current is 1.5 A.

Hence, the voltage difference across the points is
